To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

caffeine at low doses increased shuttle and operating behaviors in rats, and that the dose that induced operating behavior was higher than that induced shuttle behavior; caffeine 120 mg.k.g-1 decreased FAD contents in caudate and increased NADH contents in some brain regions, and caffeine 60 mg/kg-1 increased FADS contents in cerebellum, brain stem and NADH contents.
caffeine has different effects on shuttle and operating behaviors in rats, caffeine has effects on dinucleotides contents and brain metabolism in some brain areas.
caffeine 30-60 mg/kg induced shuttling behavior and increased NADH content in some brain areas, but caffeine 60-120 mg/kg decreased FAD content and pterin contents in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of caffeine on shuttling behavior, operating behavior, brain metabolism in rats.
the effects of caffeine on shuttle and operating behaviors in rats, and the possible mechanism of the effects of caffeine is discussed.
effects of caffeine on shuttling, operating behaviors, contents of dinucleotide and pterins of brain areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
caffeine 30-60 mg.kg(-1) increased brain metabolism and induced shuttling behavior, but caffeine 120 mg.k-1 inhibited brain metabolism and induced operating behavior.
caffeine at low doses (30 mg.kg- 1) induced shuttle behavior, at middle doses (60 mg.kg -1) induced operating behavior, at high doses (120 mg.kg - 1) inhibited both behaviors.

caffeine 30, 60 mg.k.g-1 induced shuttle behavior; caffeine 60, 90, 120 mg/kg induced operating behavior; caffeine 120 mg.k.g- induced both shuttle and operating behaviors; caffeine 60-120 mg/kg induced decrease of pterin and increase of biopterin contents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caffeine at lower dose induced shuttle and operating behaviors, and increased brain metabolism; caffeine at higher dose decreased brain metabolism.
caffeine induced shuttling and/or operating behavior by increasing FAD content, but caffeine induced operating behavior by increasing NADH content and decreasing pterin contents in some areas.
caffeine could affect shuttle, operating behaviors and brain metabolism, but the mechanisms of these effects are not clear.
The main takeaway from our work is that

caffeine can induce both shuttling behavior and operating behavior in rats, the dose of caffeine to augment shuttle behavior is lower than that to induce operating behavior, caffeine can affect brain metabolism and contents of dinucleotide, and caffeine can increase biopterin contents.
caffeine has different effects on shuttling behavior and operating behavior, caffeine may affect the energy metabolism in brain.
caffeine has a significant influence on shuttle, operating behavior, and brain metabolism.
